t: From a blank sheet to your first part for the 3D printer, in five minutes, with no account and nothing to install. layerling is a design program for 3D printing that runs right in your browser. You build a part from simple shapes, cut holes into it, round the edges and send it to your slicer. There is nothing to install and nothing to sign up for. What you build stays on your computer. The start page of layerling: "Create new 3D design" at the top, your designs and the quick guide below.

Open layerling.com. On the start page click „Utwórz nowy projekt 3D”. The editor opens with an empty workplane, the grid on which everything takes shape. If you already have a file to continue with, use „Otwórz projekt lub zaimportuj geometrię”. That works for layerling designs (.lyl) as well as STL, OBJ, 3MF, STEP or SVG files. All your designs later appear on the start page with a preview picture. They are kept in your browser's storage and saved automatically after every change, so there is no save button. How to pack designs into a file and pass them on is covered in Files and saving.

The editor with two shapes on the workplane. The ribbon on top, the camera controls on the left, the settings of the selected shape on the right. On top is the ribbon. It is sorted by task: „Schowek”, „Historia”, „Kształty”, „Widoczność”, „Łączenie”, „Modyfikuj”, „Rozmieść”, „Zarządzaj” and „Pomoc”. Hover over an icon to see its name. Wherever you see a small question mark, for example in a shape's settings, in the shape library or in the tool panels, it leads straight to the matching chapter of this guide. In the middle lies the workplane. This is where you place shapes, pull them into form and see the result. On the right appear the settings of the selected shape: colour, dimensions, position and whatever else makes up the shape. Typing numbers is more exact than dragging. On the left are the camera controls with the view cube above them. They move you around the scene, more in View and workplane. At the very top you switch between „Edytor 3D” and „Szkic”, rename the design and choose language and colour scheme.

As an example, we build a cube with a hole. Click „Dodaj kształt” in the ribbon and pick „Prostopadłościan”. The shape now hangs on your mouse pointer. A click on the workplane sets it down. On the right, set the dimensions, for example 40 mm long, 40 mm wide and 20 mm high. Place a „Walec” in the middle the same way, 14 mm across and 30 mm high. It should be taller than the cube so it reaches all the way through. Select the cylinder and click „Otwór” on the right. It turns see-through: the solid has become a tool that takes material away. Select both shapes and click „Grupuj”. The cube now has a hole. The cylinder is a hole and sticks out of the top of the cube. After grouping, the cube has a bore. This is how bores, slots and pockets are made. The chapter Solids and holes explains it in detail.

When you open layerling again after an update, a card on the start page lists what has been added since you were last here: every version since then, the newest first. After a long absence you scroll down inside the card. Below them, „Pokaż wcześniejsze wersje ({count})” adds the versions from before your last visit too. Close it with „Rozumiem” and it stays away until the next update. „Co nowego?” in the footer of the start page shows the latest additions again at any time. The browser remembers the last version you saw, and nothing about you leaves it. On a copy of layerling on your own computer or server, the notice "Update available" has a button, „Podgląd: co przynosi aktualizacja?”, that lists what the update brings before you install it. The list is fetched from GitHub only when you press the button.

When your part is done, click „Eksportuj”, choose STL or 3MF and download the file. Open it in your slicer, for example Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer or Cura. If you choose your printer in the settings, you can see while building whether the part fits on the print bed. More in Printing. Tip: If you come from Tinkercad you will find your way quickly: plate, shapes, solid and hole, group, align and mirror work almost the same. What is new is mostly chamfer and fillet, hollowing, threads and sketches.
Moving around the scene, looking straight on, and placing new shapes on any surface you like.

With the mouse: What you do What happens drag with the right button rotate the view click the right button on a body, a menu with the most used commands: duplicate, hole or solid, group, hide, lock, delete and more; on empty space Paste and Select all drag with the middle button move the view mouse wheel zoom in and out hold Ctrl and drag with the left button also moves the view How fast the wheel zooms is set with „Szybkość przybliżania” in the settings, under „Wygląd”: a slider from 1 to 10, 5 to begin with. On a tablet or phone, two fingers zoom (spread and pinch) and move the view (slide together). One finger works on the design, just like the left mouse button. To rotate with one finger, switch on „Obracaj widok jednym palcem” in the camera bar. That switch only shows on devices with a touch screen. A graphics tablet with a pen behaves like a mouse: the tip is the left button, the barrel button on the pen the right one, for turning the view and for the menu. The tablet's hotkeys can be set in its driver to layerling's keyboard shortcuts.

The cube in the top left shows where you are looking. A click on one of its sides jumps to the straight view from top, bottom, front, back, left or right. A click on a corner of the cube looks at the model diagonally from that corner, and a click near an edge looks from that edge, between two sides; the spot lights up while the pointer is on it. The number keys 1 to 6 give the straight views too. Hold Shift with them and the view also zooms to the selection, as Shift+F does. Drag the cube to turn the view around, just like dragging with the right mouse button. With nothing selected, the arrow keys turn the view as well: 15° a press, 90° with Shift. They turn the model the way they point - → turns its front to the right, ↑ tilts its front upwards. If something is selected, the arrows move it; click on empty space first to turn the view. On a touch screen this works with one finger, without switching on „Obracaj widok jednym palcem”.

At the left edge is a narrow bar. From the top: „Widok początkowy” brings the whole scene back into view. The key is F or Home. „Wyśrodkuj widok na zaznaczeniu” zooms to the selection (Shift+F). „Przybliż” and „Oddal” zoom step by step, as do the keys + and −. „Widok ortogonalny” switches to a flat view in which parallel edges stay parallel. For measuring and lining up edges that is often more comfortable than the perspective view. O switches back and forth, and a second click returns. „Ukryj płaszczyznę roboczą” (the eye over a grid) hides the plate with its grid, so you can look at the underside of a design from below. Only the view changes: new shapes still land on the workplane. A second click shows it again. „Umieść płaszczyznę roboczą”, the tape measure and the framing square are tools of their own, covered below and in Measuring and notes. The small arrow at the very top of the bar hides it if it gets in the way. A design opens the way you left it: the angle, zoom and position of the view are kept with it in this browser, so you continue where you stopped, also after going Home or closing the page. A saved file (.lyl) carries the view along, so it opens in it elsewhere too. The view is not part of the undo history.

„Widok przekroju”, the last button in the bar (the cut tool), cuts the view open along a plane so you can check walls, cavities and parts that fit into each other. Nothing is cut for real: the design, its files and every export stay whole. Choose the axis the plane stands across: X (width), Y (depth) or Z (height), as in the position fields. The plane starts in the middle of your design. „Zgrubnie” moves the plane across the whole design, „Dokładnie” moves it a little either side of where it stands, for tenths of a millimetre. You can also type the position. The button beside the axes shows the other side of the cut, „Wyśrodkuj” puts the plane back in the middle, and „Pokaż płaszczyznę cięcia” hides the blue plane. You can click and select what the cut lays open, inner walls included. „Płaszczyzna robocza tutaj” puts the workplane on the cut. It lies on the plane of the section and faces out of the body that stays, like the face a cut leaves. If you then switch to the sketch, it starts exactly there, and the faint outline shows the cut, which you can draw along and snap to. That is how you sketch a lid that fits the cavity you opened with the section, for example. The button beside the axes chooses which side stays, and with it which way the workplane faces. You put the workplane back on the base plate as usual. „Mierz” measures right on the cut: the outline shows in blue, and two clicks on it give the distance, plus its parts along the plane's two axes. Both points snap to the outline, corners first. When the second click lands anywhere on the opposite wall, it snaps square to the first point - so you read wall thickness, gaps and clearance without aiming exactly. A third click starts the next measurement, Esc ends measuring. Moving the plane clears the measurement. „Przekrój jako SVG” saves the outlines on the cutting plane as an SVG at 1:1, for a laser, a plotter, a template or a gasket. An X cut is seen from the right, a Y cut from the front, a Z cut from above. As in the export, only visible bodies go in, holes are already taken off, and bodies of the same colour are joined into one outline. Each colour stays its own path without a fill, so laser software keeps them apart as layers. The panel hangs on its button. If it covers something, drag it by its title bar anywhere on the workplane; it opens there next time too. Double-click the title bar or drop it at the button to put it back. Esc closes the panel; the cut stays until you switch it off or go back to the design overview. While it is on, its button stays highlighted. Anything you place on the side that is cut away only shows once you switch the cut off.

New shapes align with the workplane. At first that is the base plate with the grid. But you can put it on any surface, to place something on a side or a sloped face. Press W or click „Umieść płaszczyznę roboczą”. Move the mouse over a face of a body. It lights up. A click puts the workplane there. Everything you add now sits on that face. Click on the empty plate instead, and the workplane lies flat at the spot you clicked, on the snap grid. New shapes and a finished sketch, a revolved one too, then appear there rather than in the middle of the plate. While the workplane lies flat on the plate like this, the plate shows only its outline: two grids in the same plane would make a flickering pattern. On a face the origin of the workplane otherwise snaps to the grid. Click close to a corner of the face and it sits exactly on that corner. Close to an edge it lies on the edge, and the grid lines up with it; that is how you choose the angle of the grid on purpose. Without a corner or an edge, the grid on a lying face runs parallel to the body, so on a turned box it is turned with it. A click beside the plate or Esc returns the workplane to the base plate. Quicker still is „Płaszczyzna robocza z powrotem na płytę bazową”: the button with the downward arrow sits in the camera bar below the eye while the workplane lies on a face. Shift+W puts it directly on the currently selected face. If you hold Shift while clicking, the plane points the other way. While a workplane sits on a face, an eye appears next to „Umieść płaszczyznę roboczą”. It hides the workplane without dropping it, for a clear look at the design: new shapes still land on that face, and rotating still turns about it. A click on the eye shows it again, and so does setting a new workplane.

The grid shows the size of the plate. At the bottom right is the snap step: moving and scaling snap in steps of that size, for example 1 mm. Make it smaller for fine work and larger for rough arranging. „Przyciągaj do siatki” in the ribbon moves the selected shapes afterwards onto the nearest grid crossing. While moving, shapes also snap to other shapes, see Selecting and arranging. Under „Pomiary” in the settings you set the „Jednostki”. With „Calowe”, layerling shows every measure in inches, on the shape, in the properties panel, on the tape measure and the ruler. The snap grid then offers steps from 1/64 to 1 inch, and the grid on the plate is drawn in inches (1/8 to 1 inch, 1/4 inch by default) with a stronger line on every whole inch. Under „Pokazuj cale jako” you choose whether inches appear as fractions like in Tinkercad (1 5/8, rounded to 1/64 inch) or as decimals (1.625) with as many decimal places as set under „Dokładność”. You can type either, "1 5/8" included. Under „Własne siatki przyciągania” in the same place you add snap steps of your own: a name and a size in millimetres, for example "Pin pitch 2.54 mm" for the spacing of DIP chips, pin headers and perfboard holes, or "MX Key Unit" with 19.05 mm for the spacing of keyboard keys. The snap step menu then offers that measure whole, halved and quartered (1 ×, ½ × and ¼ ×), so shapes can be moved by one pitch, half a pitch or a quarter pitch. Custom steps are kept with the design and go along with „Ustaw jako domyślne”. Size, grid width and colour of the plate are changed in the settings (the cogwheel in the ribbon): the areas are „Wygląd”, „Pomiary”, „Płaszczyzna robocza”, „Domyślne kształtów” and „Historia”. Under „Wygląd” you find switches such as „Uruchamiaj edytor w widoku perspektywicznym” and „Pokazuj cienie”, under „Płaszczyzna robocza” „Pokazuj siatkę”. The colours of the work area are set under „Wygląd” too: „Tło okna (motyw jasny)” and „Płaszczyzna robocza pod siatką (motyw jasny)” for the light theme (the dark themes keep their own), next to the grid colour under „Płaszczyzna robocza”. There you also choose whether the darker grid line comes every 5 or every 10 grid steps („Ciemniejsza linia siatki co”) and give it a colour of its own with „Kolor ciemniejszej linii”; the centre cross and the plate border take it too. Every line of the grid grows wider as you zoom in, as in Tinkercad, and stays visible as you zoom out; if that is too much for you, switch off „Linie siatki grubieją przy przybliżaniu” and the lines stay one pixel wide at every zoom, as in the sketch. In the colour field, Enter takes a typed hex value. „Linie krawędzi na wszystkich bryłach” draws an outline on every body, in the colour of „Kolor linii krawędzi” (black to begin with, as in Tinkercad): it helps when dark colours run into each other. It is off by default, and very large imported meshes are left out. The grid always runs through the origin, so the stronger lines lie on the axes whatever the plate measures. „Strzałki osi” (on by default) draws three arrows at the back left corner of the plate: X in red to the right, Y in green to the back and Z in blue upwards, the way the position fields count. That is the right-hand rule Tinkercad, CAD programs and the slicers use too. With the workplane on a face they follow it. Switch them off here if they are in your way. Two sliders under „Wygląd” set how the bodies are lit. „Siła cieni” says how dark the cast shadows are, and „Kontrast cieniowania” moves light from the even ambient light to the main light: towards "punchy" the shaded sides get darker and the shadows show more, towards "soft" everything gets flatter. At the top end the contrast gets very strong, so shaded sides and shadows turn really dark. „Miękkość cieni” makes the edges of the shadows soft instead of crisp. „Kierunek światła” turns the main light round the plate (0° from the front, 90° from the right), and „Wysokość światła” lifts it; at 90° it stands straight above the plate as in Tinkercad, and the shadows fall right under the bodies. „Przywróć światło i cienie” puts everything back. „Klasyczny wygląd” sets the work area up as Tinkercad shows it: white ground, a pale blue millimetre grid with a darker line every centimetre, black edge lines, light from above with soft shadows. Every value can still be changed on its own afterwards. All of them start as layerling always looked, and what suits you depends on your monitor. The sketch view has its own colours: „Szkic: tło okna (motyw jasny)” for the window round the sheet, „Szkic: obszar pod siatką (motyw jasny)” for the sheet under the grid, and „Szkic: kolor siatki (motyw jasny)”, all for the light theme. „Szkic jak obszar roboczy” takes over the work area's three colours in one click. The settings under Appearance: background and workplane colours for the light theme, and the switch for edge lines on all bodies. Three dark bodies with edge lines switched on: the outlines keep them apart. The editor in the dark colour scheme. You set the colour scheme at the top right: System, Light, Dark or Graphite. „Rozmiar paska narzędzi” under „Wygląd” makes the buttons of the ribbon on top, its shape menu and the camera controls on the left smaller or larger: „Mały”, „Średni” (as it always was) or „Duży”. Small leaves more room for the workplane on a laptop; large is easier to hit on a big screen or with a finger. With large buttons the groups of the ribbon go onto a second row when the window is too narrow for them. The size is kept in this browser and holds for every design. Tip: Stop rotating the view when you fit parts together exactly. Use the number keys to go to the straight view from top or front and press O for the flat display. Then you see at once whether two edges are really flush.

layerling calculates and draws everything in your browser. On an older computer, with a weak graphics card or on several large screens the view can therefore feel sluggish. This helps: „Tryb szybki” under „Wygląd” turns off at once everything that costs the view a lot: shadows, edge lines on all bodies and the camera's inertia. It also draws the view at the screen's own resolution only, which on high-resolution screens is up to four times fewer pixels. Your own settings are kept and apply again as soon as you turn it off. The camera keeps turning: When you let go of the mouse after turning, the view turns on for a moment and slows down gently. That is on purpose, not stutter. If you are used to Tinkercad or Fusion 360, turn off „Kamera obraca się dalej” under „Wygląd”, and the view stops at once. Single switches: Without fast mode you can also turn off just „Pokazuj cienie” or „Linie krawędzi na wszystkich bryłach”. Use the graphics card: In Chrome open chrome://gpu (in Edge edge://gpu). Next to "WebGL" it should say "Hardware accelerated". If it says "Software only", hardware acceleration is off in the browser's settings. On Windows you can also pick "High performance" for the browser under Settings → System → Display → Graphics, so it uses the real graphics card and not the weaker one in the processor. Simplify large imported meshes: A model of many hundred thousand triangles slows any view down. How to thin it out is in the chapter on files, under "Simplifying an imported mesh". Close other tabs: Every open layerling tab and every other 3D page shares the same graphics card.

The shape library, dimensions by number and by handle, colour, rotating, tapering and twisting. Every part in layerling starts with a shape. From them you build everything else: shapes complement each other, cut each other out or are joined into a new shape.

Click „Dodaj kształt” in the ribbon. The shape library opens. The shape library. Every little picture is rendered from the shape's real geometry. Pick a shape. It now hangs on the mouse pointer and lands where you click. Move it over a body and it lies down on the face under the pointer, sloped ones too, like Cruise in Tinkercad; over the empty plate it lands on the workplane. Esc cancels placing. A tool that waits for a click, such as the tape measure, the framing square, a note, „Umieść płaszczyznę roboczą”, „Połóż płasko na ścianie” or the edge tools, is switched off when you pick a shape, so the click places the shape. The other way round, switching one of those tools on puts the shape down again. If you would rather have the shape appear in the middle of the plate, you can switch off placing by click in the settings (area „Wygląd”, switch „Prowadź nowy kształt za kursorem przy dodawaniu”). What the library offers: Basic shapes: „Prostopadłościan”, „Zaokrąglony prostopadłościan”, „Walec”, „Kapsuła”, „Elipsa”, „Wielokąt” (three to twenty-four sides), „Kula”, „Stożek”, „Piramida” (with three to twenty-four sides, so three-sided too), „Klin”, „Okrągły dach”, „Półkula” and „Torus”. Tubes: „Rura” and „Wygięta rura”, made of up to twelve straight pieces with bends in between, and the „Przejście profili” from one outline to another, say from square to round. Decorative shapes: „Gwiazda”, „Serce” and „Półksiężyc”. Lettering: „Tekst”, also along a circular arc. More in Text. Mechanics: „Gwint” (threaded rod, screw, nut and tapped hole), „Sprężyna”, „Koło zębate” and the „Radełko” for grips. More in Threads and mechanics. For constructions: the print-in-place „Zawias”, „Jaskółczy ogon”, the „Otwór łezkowy” for horizontal holes, the „Pogłębienie walcowe” and „Pogłębienie stożkowe” for screw heads and the „Linijka”, which is only a measuring tool and never shows up in an export. You get a triangle in two ways: the „Wielokąt” with three sides is an isosceles triangle, the "Roof" of Tinkercad, and the „Klin” is a right triangle. Both are true triangular prisms. For a triangular hole, copy the shape, make the copy smaller, mark it as a hole and line it up with „Wyśrodkuj na płaszczyźnie roboczej” or „Wyrównaj”. Both work with the shape's bounding box, the smallest box that encloses it, so a halved square still counts as a whole square. The command search (Ctrl+K) also finds both shapes under "triangle" or "roof". The „Kapsuła” can be narrower at one end than at the other, say for a guard over a belt between two pulleys. Under „Właściwości” set „Mniejszy koniec (średnica)”; the large end is as wide as the capsule, and the sides run straight from one arc to the other. „Rozstaw środków” is the distance between the two arcs' centres, that is how far apart the pulleys are. Change the small end and the centre distance stays, the capsule getting longer or shorter. The tapered capsule stays an exact body too, for fillets and STEP.

As soon as a shape is selected, its settings appear on the right. At the top is the name; the pencil beside it („Zmień nazwę”) lets you type a new one. Enter keeps it, Esc cancels, and an empty name brings back the shape's default name. Further right, the padlock locks the shape against accidental moving and the eye hides it. The arrow on the far left folds the settings down to their title bar. The settings sit docked at the right edge. If they cover something you want to see, drag them by their title bar and they float wherever you drop them; they stay there for the next shape too. Drop them back at the top right, or double-click the title bar, and they dock again. While they float or are folded down, the snap step moves from the bottom of the settings to the bottom right of the workplane. The settings of a cylinder: solid or hole, diameter and height as a number and as a slider. „Bryła” or „Otwór”: A solid stays, a hole takes material away. A click on „Bryła” opens the colours; colours of your own that you mix there wait under „Ostatnio używane” afterwards, the last eight. More in Solids and holes. „Przezroczysty”: Lets you see through the body, for example to spot a shape behind it. „Wielokolorowy”: For a group only. Switched on, every part of the group shows in its own colour, also in a group that was cut with holes into one body (the walls a hole leaves take the colour of the body they were cut into). Picking a colour for the group switches it off and colours the whole group. Bundles always keep their parts' colours. In a 3MF export every part keeps its colour, so the slicer can map the parts onto filaments; OBJ carries the colours on its points, so the border between two colours is a little rougher there. „Właściwości”: The dimensions and everything that belongs to this shape. For a cylinder the diameter, the height and the number of sides. For a gear the teeth, for a spring the turns. A value you have moved away from its default gets a small arrow next to its name: a click takes just that value back, whatever else you did since, unlike Undo. Dragged with the mouse, the slider of a length snaps to the snap step, so a height comes out in whole millimetres (not with the grid off, and not on short sliders); a typed value and the arrow keys on the slider stay exact. „Zapisz jako domyślne” at the bottom makes the current values the start values of this kind of shape (the same as „Domyślne kształtów” in the settings), and „Przywróć domyślne” goes back to the app's own. „Zmień w elipsę”: Only on a cylinder. A cylinder is always round: it has one diameter, and every handle changes both sides together. For an oval, click this and it becomes an „Elipsa” - the same body, whose length and width you then set one by one. A cylinder with a chamfer, a fillet or a wall, or a turned or grouped one, cannot be changed this way; take the „Elipsa” from the start for those. „Zwężenie”: Different sizes at the top and bottom, for example for a slope or a funnel. „Skręt i pochylenie”: Twists the top against the bottom or shifts it sideways. That gives twisted columns and leaning towers. A group of an orange block, a blue peg and a hole, cut into one body. With Multicolor switched on, the peg stays blue, the block orange, and the walls of the hole take the block's colour. Taper and twist work on almost every shape. Only the gear, thread, spring, knurl, hinge, pyramid, bent tube, teardrop, the screw-head cutters and the ruler leave them out: they have fixed measures of their own or, like the pyramid, a top of their own already. A cone whose top radius and height were changed: a small arrow next to each takes the value back, and the two buttons at the bottom save or reset the defaults of the shape. A tapered or leaning box, cylinder, ellipse, polygon, tube or ring keeps its exact shape, and so do the capsule, star, heart, crescent, dovetail and a rounded box without rounded top and bottom edges: chamfers and fillets work on it as on the plain shape, and the STEP export writes it. The same holds for a twisted shape: its section turns exactly as it rises, and the sides wind evenly from bottom to top. Typing is more exact than dragging. All number fields take millimetres, but also percentages: type "50 %" into a width of 40 mm and you get 20 mm. They calculate too: "15*3", "120-2*4" or "(40+2)/2" give 45, 112 and 21; x works instead of *. The field remembers the calculation, in the Properties panel as well as in the dimension boxes around the selected body: click into it again later and the formula stands there instead of the number, as long as the value still matches it, and you change it in place, "(140+2)/2" becoming "(40+6)/2". Drag the body by a handle or scale it and the formula no longer fits, so the field shows just the number again.

h: How round is round? The side count
t: Round shapes such as cylinder, cone, tube, ellipse or the bores have the switch „Boki zależne od rozmiaru” and the slider „Boki” in their properties. The „Torus” has two sliders: „Boki pierścienia” around the ring and „Kroki rury” around the tube. They follow the size there too until you hold them, so a large torus shows no facets. The reason: for the view and for STL, 3MF and OBJ, layerling draws a circle as a polygon of many small sides. The more sides, the smoother it is, and the more triangles it takes. Where the side count matters In the export for the slicer (STL, 3MF, OBJ). A cylinder with few sides arrives there as a polygon. When bodies and holes are combined. A bore cut by a hole with few sides is angular in the finished part. That includes screw holes. In the view. Many very fine shapes slow the editor down. Where it does not matter For the STEP export. It writes the round shape, not the polygon. For chamfers and fillets („Fazowanie”, „Zaokrąglenie”) as long as the shape stays round. That is the case when you have not set a side count, when the count is at least the shape's default, or when the polygon strays at most 0,05 mm from the circle. The default is 96 sides for cylinder, ellipse, tube and cone, 64 for the „Okrągły dach”, 24 steps for the „Kula”, 32 for the „Półkula”, 96 sides and 24 steps for the „Torus”, and a „Jakość” of 32 for a round „Wygięta rura”. For a thread, a spring or a helical gear. The edge tool and the STEP export take its exact body; its „Jakość” only sets how finely it is drawn. Where it matters again For chamfers and fillets on a shape with few sides. If you set the side count below the default, the edge tool takes the shape as it is drawn: a cylinder with 6 sides stays a hexagonal bar, and the fillet runs round its six edges. That is how you can build, for instance, a nut pocket with rounded corners. For a round shape, leave „Boki zależne od rozmiaru” on. How to use it Leave „Boki zależne od rozmiaru” on. Then layerling picks the side count from the diameter so that the polygon strays at most 0,005 mm from the true circle, far below what a printer resolves. Small shapes get at least 24 sides, large ones more. Fewer sides you take when you want a polygon on purpose (but there is the „Wielokąt” for that) or when the editor gets slow with very many round shapes. More sides you hardly ever need. Only on very large round parts, when you see edges in the STL. For parts you only treat with edges or hand on as STEP, the side count does not matter.

Besides the settings there are handles on the shape itself: The corners and edges make the shape larger or smaller. Hold Shift while dragging a corner to scale width, depth and height together and keep the proportions; hold Alt to scale from the center instead of the opposite corner. Without a keyboard, or if you do not want to hold a key, switch on „Zachowaj proporcje” at the top of the properties: then the corners always keep the proportions, and typing one of width, depth or height scales the other two by the same factor. The setting is remembered. The arrow on top changes the height, the handle in the middle lifts or lowers the shape. The curved arrows rotate it. The numbers beside the shape show the dimensions. A click on one opens a field in which you type the number you want. With Enter the shape grows from the edge opposite the number, as when you drag; with Alt+Enter it grows round its middle, so a shape that was aligned with another stays aligned. That holds for width and length; the height always grows upward from the underside. The fields in the properties on the right keep the middle without a key. A click on a corner (without dragging) opens width and depth together. Type the first, press Tab for the second and Enter to apply both. Esc cancels. Once a shape is turned by right angles, for instance laid on its side with „Połóż płasko na ścianie”, the fields in the properties are named after the direction each measure runs in now: „Wysokość” is what goes up, „Szerokość” runs along X and „Długość” along Y. Typing the height of a shape lying down therefore changes the vertical measure, and its underside stays on the plate. A shape tilted at any other angle shows its own measures in the fields, and a note below says so. Without the mouse, use the keyboard: the arrow keys move the selection by one snap step (0.1 mm when the grid is off), with Shift by five, or by ten if you set „Ciemniejsza linia siatki co” to 10 „kroki siatki: {count}” in the settings under „Wygląd”: as far as the next darker line, as in Tinkercad. They follow the view: → moves to where the screen's right is, ↑ away from you, even after turning the plate. Push a shape out of the picture and the view moves along. Ctrl+↑ and Ctrl+↓ raise and lower it. R rotates by 45°, Shift+R by 22.5°. D drops the selection onto the workplane. The handles pull a shape as large as your plate, at least 220 mm wide and deep. Typing a number in the properties goes beyond that, and a shape made that large does not shrink back when you grab it again. A ceiling of your own per shape is set in the settings under „Domyślne kształtów” with „Własny limit rozmiaru”. The snap step is at the bottom right of the editor and can be changed at any time.

„Kopiuj”, „Wklej” and „Duplikuj” are in the ribbon („Schowek”). Ctrl+D duplicates a selection. layerling remembers how you last moved or rotated the copy and applies the same again on the next duplicate. That produces a row of holes or steps in a few key presses. For regular arrangements there is also the pattern, described in Selecting and arranging. Tip: If a shape refuses to take the size you want, it is often the limits for new shapes. Under „Domyślne kształtów” in the settings you decide how each shape starts and how large it may get.

A holder, a grip or a base plate you need again and again goes into the „Własne kształty”. They sit at the top of the shape library, above the „Podstawowe kształty”, and fold away with their arrow. Select one or more bodies, holes, groups or an imported model included. Open the shape library and click „Zapisz zaznaczenie”. Enter a name and confirm with „Zapisz”. In any design, a click on the tile inserts the shape, like any other shape. You can also drag the tile onto the workplane; it then lands where you let go. Several bodies come back together, placed as they stood to each other, and stay selectable one by one. The pencil on a tile renames it, the bin removes it after asking. Shapes already inserted into designs stay as they are. The „Własne kształty” live in this browser, apart from the designs, and are there again the next time you start. „Kopia zapasowa wszystkiego” on the start page backs them up with the designs, and opening the backup brings both back. To take only the shapes to another browser, „Kopia zapasowa własnych kształtów” (the arrow pointing down) saves them as a ZIP file and „Wczytaj kształty” (the arrow pointing up) brings them back there. „Wczytaj kształty” also takes single .lyl designs; each one becomes a shape. Shapes already there are not added twice.

With the shared server store switched on, the section shows two groups: „Na serwerze” and „W tej przeglądarce”. When saving you choose where the shape goes; the server is chosen to start with. There it lives in the folder Custom shapes, as a .lyl file of its own with a picture, ready on every device that reaches the server. The cloud on a browser tile puts that shape on the server; it is then no longer kept twice. The Custom shapes folder shows on the start page as well. Open a shape there like a design, change it, and it is saved automatically like any design on the server; the next insert takes the new version. As the server store has no login, everyone who reaches the server sees the same shapes.

Should a pattern, a logo or lettering go onto a cup, a can or a tube? First lay it flat on the plate, as an imported SVG or as text for example, the way it should look from above. Then wrap it around a cylinder in the shape's settings under „Owiń wokół walca”: Open „Owiń wokół walca” and enter the „Średnica” of the cylinder wall, such as the outside diameter of your cup. Tenths of a millimetre work too, such as 63.5. Click „Owiń”. What ran from left to right now runs around the cylinder, the back edge becomes the top, and the thickness stands out of the wall. Select the wrapped shape and the cylinder and centre both, left to right and front to back. The middle of the wrapped shape is the cylinder's axis, so it then sits right on its wall. For an engraving, switch on „Do wewnątrz (grawer)”: the thickness then goes into the wall. Make the shape a hole, centre it and group it with the cylinder. A shape that is wrapped already is a mesh of the wrapped thing and cannot be wrapped again: undo the wrapping, or wrap the flat original once more with another diameter. The result is a mesh like an imported model. Undo lays the shape flat again; for another diameter, undo first and wrap again. It cannot go further than once around the cylinder; then layerling names the smallest diameter that fits.
Selecting shapes, finding them in the object list, aligning, mirroring, rotating, laying flat on a face and multiplying in patterns.

A click on a shape selects it. With Shift you add more or take them away again. A click on empty space clears the selection, and so does Esc. Drag a frame on the empty workplane to select everything it touches; with Shift held, the frame adds what was not selected and takes away what was. And Ctrl+A selects all visible bodies. What is in your way you hide („Ukryj zaznaczone”, Ctrl+H). Hidden shapes stay in the design, they are just not visible and stay out of the export; the export window says beforehand how many there are. Ctrl+Shift+H brings them all back. What should stay put you lock with the padlock at the top of the settings or with Ctrl+L. A locked shape cannot be moved, resized, turned, recoloured or deleted: its handles turn grey, a padlock shows beside the arrow on top, and the tools that would change it are greyed out. Hovering a handle still shows its sizes, and a key that would change it says "Object locked". While one locked shape is in the selection, nothing changes for the others either. Hiding, renaming, copying and duplicating still work.

With many parts it is easy to lose track in the view. The object list („Pokaż listę obiektów” or Ctrl+Shift+O) shows all shapes as a list. The object list: the group "Group" with two parts and a sphere beside it. A folder icon opens the group. A click on an entry selects the shape, including parts inside a group. With Shift held you add more entries or take them away again, just as in the view. The arrows fold groups open and shut. The label shows whether a part is „Bryła” or „Otwór”. Padlock and eye lock and hide single parts. „Zmień nazwę” gives a part a name of its own; the pencil beside the name at the top of the settings does the same for the selected shape. Sensible names help enormously in larger designs. The search field finds shapes by name and by kind, so also "cylinder" or "hole". It also looks inside groups, however deeply nested: a group holding a match stays in the list and folds open to show the matching parts and the groups that lead to them. A group found by its own name shows all its parts when you open it. The arrow on the far left of the title bar folds the list down to its title bar and back. The list sits docked just right of the view cube. Drag it by its title bar to put it anywhere on the workplane; it passes underneath the view cube and the camera bar. Drop it back beside the view cube, or double-click the title bar, and it docks again. Where it was and whether it was folded are remembered in this browser.

The card „Pozycja” in the properties panel shows where the selected body stands, and you can type it: „X” and „Y” are the middle of its box on the plate, with the same signs as the distances shown on the workplane, and „Z (wysokość)” is the height of its underside. X counts to the right, Y towards the back and Z up, by the right-hand rule as in Tinkercad and CAD programs; the axis arrows on the plate show the directions. The values go in the unit you set, and the sliders reach as far as dragging does.

You can drag a shape past the edge of the plate and leave it there, about one plate width beyond each side, to keep it for later. The arrow keys move it as far as you like. A parked part still belongs to the design and goes into the export with everything else. To leave it out, hide it or export only the selection. If you have picked a printer, layerling warns at export when something sits outside its plate.

When you drag a shape across the workplane, it snaps to other shapes: its left, right, front or back edge or its centre lands exactly on an edge or centre of another shape. A pink guide line shows what it is holding on to. That way two parts sit flush side by side or centred one behind the other without typing numbers. It works with the grid switched off, too. Hold Shift while dragging to keep the move on one axis: the shape follows whichever direction, X or Y, you have dragged further in, and leaves the other alone. Best press Shift once you are already dragging; on a shape that is not selected yet, a click with Shift only adds it to the selection. With Alt already held when the drag begins, you drag a copy, as in Tinkercad: the shape stays where it is and the copy lands where you let go. Pressing Alt only on the way pauses snapping; the shape then follows the grid only. A copy, too, snaps only once you let go of Alt on the way. To switch snapping off for good, use the grid menu in the bottom right („Przyciągaj do kształtów”) or the settings. For now only moving on the normal workplane snaps, not lifting and not resizing.

Two or more selected shapes are lined up with „Wyrównaj”: points appear around the selection for left, centre and right, front, centre and back, and top, centre and bottom. A click on a point moves all shapes there. If you first click one of the selected shapes, it stays in place and the others line up with it. A locked shape in the selection is that fixed shape by itself. Left, right, front, back, top and bottom go by the box round a shape; the centre of a triangle, a pentagon or a star is its own middle, so a hole centred on one sits in the middle of the shape and not of its box. A shape turned at an angle, say by 45°, has its box round it to line up with, not its own edges. To line up with the edges, set a workplane on a face of that shape first („Umieść płaszczyznę roboczą”, then click the face): the points then stand on the axes of that plane, and the shapes are measured and moved along them, as in Tinkercad. Reset the workplane to line up along the plate again. Align shows the possible targets as dots around the selection. The key is L. Esc cancels.

„Odbicie lustrzane” (M, or right-click the selection and choose it) flips the selection across a plane: „lewo-prawo”, „przód-tył” or „góra-dół”. Click the matching axis arrow. That is handy for symmetric parts: build one half, copy it and mirror the copy.

You rotate with the curved arrows on the shape, with the numbers in the settings or with R in 45° steps. When you drag on the rotation circle, the turn snaps to every tick, that is every 22.5°; hold Shift for finer steps, and extra ticks appear every 11.25°. Drag outside the circle to turn freely in 1° steps, or in 45° steps with Shift. Normally the selection turns about its centre. Sometimes it should not, for example when a tilted tube is to be turned further at its end. For that there is „Ustaw punkt obrotu”: afterwards click on a face. A flat face supplies its centre, for example the axis of a tube end. The selection now turns about that point. A second click on the tool removes it again. The angles stay with the body. In its settings, „Obrót” shows them as „Wokół X”, „Wokół Y” and „Wokół Z (wysokość)”, named like the position: Y runs across the plate, Z is up. Type an angle there and the body turns to it - about its centre, or about its own pivot if it has one. While a turned body is selected, its angles also show below it on the workplane; „Pokazuj kąty obróconych brył” in the settings switches that off. A body turned about two axes: its angles stand under it, and the Rotation card in its settings takes them as numbers. With one body selected, the pivot belongs to that body: select other parts and come back, and it is still there. It moves, turns and scales with the body, is saved in the project and comes back with Undo. Under „Pozycja” the pivot has its own X, Y and Z, which you can type or nudge, and „Usuń” takes it away. You can also drag the pivot's red marker with the mouse: it slides over the surface of the bodies and snaps to corners, edge midpoints and edges, so a hinge pin lands exactly on a corner. With several bodies selected the pivot is only for that selection, and a new selection removes it.

Should a part lie on its best side for printing? Select it, click „Połóż płasko na ścianie” and then the face that should go down. While you move the pointer over the part, the face under it lights up, so you see which one you are about to pick; turn the view to check the other sides. The part turns so that this face rests on the workplane. Two parts should meet face to face, or line up flush? Select the part that should move, click „Wyrównaj ściany”, then click its face and after that the face of the other part. In the panel, „Ściana do ściany” puts the faces against each other (back to back, touching), „Na równo” lays them in one plane side by side; „Szczelina” leaves room between them, for example for clearance. „Wyrównaj” moves the part: it turns the shortest way until the faces are parallel - not at all if they already are - and then slides only towards the other face, so it keeps its place sideways. The other part stays where it is, and one Undo takes it all back. The Align faces panel: the part that moves is picked, a face of the other part comes next, then face to face or flush, and an optional gap. Just as simple are „Opuść na płaszczyznę roboczą” (D), which drops the selection onto the workplane, and „Wyśrodkuj na płaszczyźnie roboczej”. C picks the selection up, like Cruise in Tinkercad: it follows the mouse pointer and lies down on the face of another body you are over, sloped ones too. A click sets it down there, Esc leaves it where it was. Its underside then rests on the face, lined up with the face's edges as a new shape would be; it keeps its own turn about its up axis. Several parts travel together and keep their spacing. Over the empty plate, C stands a tilted part upright on the workplane again.

For hole grids, bolt circles and rings of teeth there is the „Szyk”. Select the shapes to be multiplied and click it in the ribbon. The pattern in "Circle" mode: the copies first appear as a preview. „Rząd”: The selection is repeated at equal distances. The row steps along all three axes at once, with „Odstęp X”, „Odstęp Y” and „Odstęp Z (wysokość)”: one of them gives a straight row, two or three a diagonal row or a staircase. A negative spacing lays the row the other way. „Okrąg”: The selection is spread around a centre. How many copies there are you set under „Liczba (z oryginałem)”, and the „Kąt całkowity” is 360° for a full circle. Choose whether the copies turn along. „Wzniesienie na kopię” lifts every copy a little more than the one before (a screw or an ascending spiral), and „Zmiana promienia na kopię” moves it further from the centre or closer to it (a flat spiral); together they give a conical spiral. Tip: first set the pivot on a face with „Ustaw punkt obrotu”, then the centre of the circle lies exactly there. The pattern in "Circle" mode with a rise and a radius change per copy: the copies climb and widen like a spiral. The copies first appear as a preview. Only „Utwórz” creates them. If the copies are holes, group them afterwards with the body they should cut into.

For vents, speaker grilles, baskets and enclosures the „Wzór otworów” spreads holes evenly over a flat face. You no longer have to make one hole, repeat it and set it onto the wall. Select exactly one body and click „Wzór otworów” in the „Modyfikuj” group of the toolbar, next to the pattern. You can also right-click the body, or find it with Ctrl+K. Click a flat face of the body. The whole flat face around your click counts, not just the triangle under the pointer. A curved face does not work: you get a hint and click a flat one instead. In the window, set how the holes look and lie: „Kształt otworu”: „Okrągły”, „Kwadratowy”, „Prostokątny”, „Sześciokątny” or „Podłużny”. Size: the „Średnica (Ø)” of a round hole, the „Długość boku” of a square one, „Szerokość” and „Wysokość” for a rectangle and a slot. For the hexagon the size is the „Średnica po narożnikach (Ø)”. „Rozstaw od środka do środka”: the distance from one hole's middle to the next. If it is smaller than the holes allow, layerling raises it to the smallest possible value so a wall stays between the holes. „Ścianka między otworami”: the same distance said another way: the wall left between two neighbouring holes, which is the wall thickness in the print. Set it and the spacing centre to centre follows, and the other way round. For hexagons, rectangles and slots layerling measures the least distance between their edges. „Układ”: „Siatka” puts the holes in rows and columns. „Przestawiony” shifts every second row by half a spacing and moves the rows closer, so every hole has neighbours at the same distance - with hexagons that makes a honeycomb. „Margines od krawędzi ściany”: the clear distance between the holes and the edge of the face. Only holes that lie wholly inside the face minus this margin are made; anything that would reach beyond it is left out. The margin also holds around openings in the face. „Głębokość”: „Przez całą bryłę” (the default) cuts through the whole wall. With „Własna głębokość” you give the depth in millimetres, for recesses, say. The holes show at once as a preview on the face and follow every value. The window says how many holes fit. „Inna ściana” chooses another face, Esc closes the tool, and like the other tool windows it moves by its title bar. Only „Utwórz” makes the holes. The holes are ordinary holes grouped with the body, just as after „Grupuj”: nothing is baked in. „Rozgrupuj” dissolves the group again and frees every hole, which you can then move, change or delete one by one. The whole thing is one step for „Cofnij”. The tool does not make more than 400 holes at once; make the holes bigger or the spacing wider then. An AI can do the same through the MCP bridge with layerling_perforate_face (see the chapter AI with MCP).

With several parts selected, the properties panel on the right shows how many there are and offers what applies to all of them together: „Bryła” or „Otwór”, one colour for all (a click on „Bryła” opens the colours) and the lock. With a mixed selection, one click makes them all solids or all holes. If any of the parts is locked, only the lock can be used. Sizes are changed with the handles, with „Skaluj o procent” or by typing a number into a size label. With several parts the number is the size of the whole selection: every part grows with it, the spaces between them too, as when you drag a handle. Solid and hole also work with a right-click or the S and H keys.

To make one or several parts larger or smaller by the same share, say all the parts of a print file by 20 %, use „Skaluj o procent”. Select the parts, right-click them and choose „Skaluj o procent”, or search for it with Ctrl+K. Under „Nowy rozmiar” you type the new size as a percentage of the current one: 120 % is a fifth larger, 50 % half the size. Width, depth and height change alike, so the proportions stay. The bottom stays where it is, so nothing sinks into the plate. With several parts you choose how they grow: „Razem”: The parts grow around their common centre, and the gaps grow with them. The whole becomes larger as if it were one part. „Każda w miejscu”: Every part grows where it stands, and the gaps between them stay the same. Only „Skaluj” changes the design, and one step back undoes it. With a locked part in the selection it does not open.
„Cofnij” (Ctrl+Z) and „Ponów” (Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y) step through your history. How many steps travel with the saved design you set in the settings under „Historia”.

„Historia”, next to undo and redo, opens a view of your history without changing anything. The work area shows the design as it was, and a slider at the bottom runs through every undo step: all the way to the right is the current state, each step to the left is one undo earlier, and states you have undone sit to the right of the current one. The arrow keys step through the states, Esc returns to the current state. You can turn and zoom the view meanwhile, but nothing can be selected or moved; the design itself stays exactly as it is. If the bar covers something, drag it away by its title bar; a double-click on it brings it back. Two things you can take along from an earlier state. „Nowy projekt z tego stanu” puts that state into a new design in the overview, named after this one with the time of that state in brackets - a design saved before layerling recorded times says "copy" instead - and with the history up to that point, so undo keeps working there. „Eksportuj ten stan” opens the usual export with that state as the design, so you can save it as STL, 3MF, STEP, a picture or a LYL file with the history up to that state. „Usuń historię” sits alone at the bottom left of the bar. After a question it removes every earlier step for good: the design keeps the state it has now (not the one shown), Undo has nothing to go back to and a file saved afterwards carries no history. Use it to share a design without its past, or to start the undo steps over. It cannot be undone; to share a file without touching your own design, choose „Brak” when exporting instead.

How simple shapes become bores, slots and pockets, and how to change a group again later. This is the most important idea in layerling, and it is quickly learned: Every shape is either a solid or a hole. A solid stays. A hole is a tool that takes material away.

Select a shape and click „Bryła” or „Otwór” in its settings. The keyboard is faster: H makes the selection a hole, S makes it a solid again. Both are also in the menu a right click on the body opens. A hole is shown see-through so you can see where it sits. T makes a body see-through, say to look into a housing; a second press makes it opaque again. It works on the whole selection: if any body is already see-through, all become opaque, otherwise all become see-through. As long as nothing is grouped, nothing happens with a hole. It just lies there and shows where something will disappear later. The cylinder is a hole. It sticks out of the top of the cube so that it cuts all the way through.

Select solids and hole(s) and click „Grupuj” (Ctrl+G). Now the holes remove the material from the solids they touch. What remains is one single new shape. The result: a cube with a bore. This is how you get: Bores: a cylinder as a hole through a body. Slots: an elongated box as a hole at the edge. Pockets: a hole that does not go all the way through. Threads in a part: a tapped hole as a hole, see Threads and mechanics. If several solids are in the group, they are joined. Two solids that touch become a single part. You can treat a group like a shape: move, rotate, colour, group again. „Rozgrupuj” (Ctrl+Shift+G) dissolves it and the individual parts are back.

A whole group can also be a solid or a hole. A simple rule applies: If the group consists only of solids (or only of holes), you switch it as a whole and its parts go along. If it contains both, say a cube with a bore, each part keeps its own state. The whole group then becomes a tool, but the bore stays a bore.

Sometimes parts should only stay together without becoming one - a white logo on a black plate for a multicolour print, say. That is what „Zestaw” (Ctrl+B) is for, as in Tinkercad. A bundle moves, turns and resizes like a shape, but nothing is merged: Every part keeps its colour and stays a solid or a hole. Holes cut nothing. In an STL, 3MF or OBJ export every part is a body of its own; in 3MF and OBJ with its colour. „Rozgrupuj” (Ctrl+Shift+G) takes a bundle apart again, E opens it for editing like a group. Chamfer, fillet and hollowing do not work on a bundle, because it is not one body: group it for that, or work on its parts one by one. If a hole in the bundle should cut after all, group the bundle (Ctrl+G).

„Część wspólna” keeps only what two or more bodies have in common. Lay two overlapping shapes on top of each other, select both and click it. That turns a cylinder and a box into a piece with one round and one straight side. A group counts the way it looks, holes included. If a hole is selected too, what remains is what all the solids share with all the holes.

If a bore turned out too small, you do not have to dissolve the group and rebuild. Select the group and click „Edytuj grupę” in its settings, the folder icon in the object list, or press E. A double click on the group does the same, as in Tinkercad, on a bundle too; if you would rather not, switch off „Dwuklik otwiera grupę lub zestaw” in the settings. A part only starts to move once the pointer has been dragged a few pixels, so a shaky click or double click does not nudge it. The parts now lie separately and you change them with every tool: make a hole larger, move a body, add a hole. The group being edited: the bar at the bottom holds Cancel and Done, and the object list shows the parts. A bar appears at the bottom of the picture. „Gotowe” rebuilds the group, with its name, its colour and its state as solid or hole. „Anuluj” puts it back untouched. If one of the parts is itself a group, you can edit it the same way, and so on as deep as your design goes. The bar shows where you are, for example "Bracket › Screw boss". „Gotowe” and „Anuluj” always finish the innermost group and take you one level back out. While you are inside a group, only the groups among its parts can be edited; to edit another one, finish first. Unlike „Rozgrupuj”, which takes a group apart for good, editing keeps the group: its name and settings stay, and you can always go back with „Anuluj”. A note: fillets and chamfers you had put on the whole group are lost on rebuild. The bar tells you so.

„Podziel” in the „Modyfikuj” area cuts the selection in two with a plane - a part too big for the print bed, say, or one you want to see the inside of. Select one or more solids or holes and click it. A translucent plane shows exactly where the cut will go; nothing changes until you apply it. „Orientacja płaszczyzny”: X makes an upright cut between left and right, Y between front and back, Z a horizontal cut between top and bottom. The axes are named as on the Position card, with Z up; Z is where the plane starts. „Położenie płaszczyzny”: where the plane crosses, with the slider or typed in. It starts in the middle. You can also drag the arrow head on the plane; the plane moves along the arrow in 0.1 mm steps. „Wybierz ścianę”, the button next to the position, lays the plane on a face: click it, then click the face. Orientation, both rotations and position are set to match. While you pick, a blue plane under the pointer shows the face it will take. A face of a body that is not selected works too, to line the cut up with it, but the plane stays within the selection. Esc stops picking and leaves the plane where it was. The two rotation sliders below turn the plane about the other two axes, up to 180° either way, for an angled cut. They can be combined. „Podziel model” or Enter makes the cut, Esc cancels (while picking a face, the first Esc only stops picking). Every object the plane crosses becomes two closed bodies, named after their side, for example "Box (Z+)" and "Box (Z-)"; objects it misses stay as they are. A hole becomes two holes, and a hollowed body keeps its cavity. Both halves stay where they were - for printing, lay each one on its cut face with „Połóż płasko na ścianie”. The halves are plain meshes: settings such as a cylinder's sides or a text's lettering are gone, so set those first. Ctrl+Z brings the original back in one step. Locked and hidden objects cannot be split.

If a shape consists of several separate pieces, such as text made of single letters, „Rozdziel części” splits it into independent shapes. Tip: Always build holes a little longer than the part they are to pass through. If the hole ends exactly flush with the face, a wafer-thin skin sometimes remains. One millimetre of overshoot makes sure.
Chamfer and fillet on chosen edges, walls of equal thickness for boxes, cups and cases.

Sharp edges rarely look good on a printed part, and they are not particularly strong either. A chamfer cuts the edge off at an angle, a fillet rounds it. Both act on the edges you click. Select the body (or the group). Click „Zaokrąglenie” or „Fazowanie” in the ribbon, press B for the fillet or Shift+B for the chamfer, or right-click the body and pick it from the menu. The body's edges light up. Click those that should be affected. Another click takes an edge out again. With Shift you add or remove a single edge. Set the size and confirm with „Zastosuj” or Enter. The "Fillet edges" tool: all sharp edges are selected, the picture shows the preview with a 4 mm radius. The panel sits at the top right. If it covers edges you want to click, drag it away by its title bar; it opens there next time too, and so do „Wydrąż” and „Szyk”. Double-click the title bar to put it back. Picking a shape from the shape list while the panel is open closes it without applying anything, and the edges you clicked are forgotten. The click then places the new shape instead of picking edges. In the panel you find: „Wszystkie ostre krawędzie” selects every edge at once, „Wyczyść” empties the selection. „Promień” for the fillet. For the chamfer you set „Odległość” or „Kąt”. „Próg ostrej krawędzi” decides which edges count as sharp at all. A value of 25° treats only clear kinks as edges and leaves flat transitions alone. „Górne krawędzie” picks only the edges along the very top of the body. It is the quick way for a cookie cutter: build the outline in a sketch as a stroke, then chamfer the top edges. „Kąt” sets how steep the chamfer is; it cannot reach further than the wall is thick. „Tylko widoczne krawędzie” hides the edges that lie behind the body from where you look. By default every edge shows through the body, which gets confusing on a busy part; with the switch on you see, and can click, only the edges facing you. Turn the view to reach the others. An edge drawn in red (see below) always shows. „Kliknięcie wybiera też krawędzie, które płynnie się przedłużają”: a click then also picks edges that flow smoothly into each other, for example all edges around a face with rounded corners. The switch only decides what a click picks: the CAD kernel always carries a chamfer or fillet on along such smoothly continuing edges. The panel tells you along how many more edges that happens. „Zachowaj rozmiar krawędzi przy zmianie rozmiaru” keeps the chamfer or fillet as large as it is, even if you scale the body later. „Jakość podglądu” („Szkicowa”, „Standardowa” or „Dokładna”) decides how finely the preview is calculated. For difficult parts „Szkicowa” is faster. While you adjust the size, layerling recalculates the preview. It can take a moment. You may keep adjusting; the last value you chose is what gets calculated. If the size is too large for the edge, layerling says so and suggests a smaller value. Often one or two millimetres less will do. At sharp angles a fillet needs more room than its radius suggests. On a small screen the panel scrolls down by itself so the message is in view. When a selection that worked fails after you click one more edge, that edge turns red and is drawn wider: it is the one that cannot be treated together with the others at this size. Click it again to take it out, or make the size smaller. If you click more edges while the message stands, the first one stays red. When there is no earlier selection that worked - the very first click, or a size you just raised - the edges that fail even on their own turn red, or all of them if it is only their combination. The edge under the pointer is drawn wider too, so you can see which one a click will pick.

A treated body can always be treated again. Select it again and open the tool - Fillet, Chamfer or Hollow, each shows the list: under „Cofnij obróbkę krawędzi” you see what is already on it. „Cofnij” takes back a single treatment. Note: if newer treatments lie on top, they go with it, and the panel tells you how many. Next to a chamfer, a fillet or a hollowing there is also „Edytuj”. It takes the treatment back the same way, but opens the tool again at once with the same edges and the old value. You change the value and apply it again: a 3 mm fillet becomes a 5 mm one without clicking the edges once more. If newer treatments lie on top, they go with it here too. This holds for edge treatments you make from now on; older ones only offer taking back, and so do single parts of a group. On a group, say a cylinder with a hole, the treated edge belongs to the finished body, not to one of its parts. So the group becomes a single body, and „Rozgrupuj” is no longer available. Take the treatment back as described above and the group returns with all its parts. The easiest way is to treat edges last. That goes for threads too: the edge tool takes a thread as its exact body, so a block with a tapped hole in it gets its edges rounded with the thread in place. Working out a thread's edges takes longer than for a plain shape, a few seconds for an M6 and about half a minute for a G1/2 pipe thread. Good to know: layerling works with real CAD geometry for fillets and chamfers, not just a triangle mesh. That is why a rounded edge is still a rounded edge in the STEP export. A part imported as STEP keeps its CAD geometry too: chamfers, fillets and hollowing work on the body from the file, however finely the part is drawn on screen. STL, OBJ and 3MF bring only triangles, and a finely drawn part can be too dense for the edge tool. If a part is also available as STEP, import that.

Boxes, cups, cases and covers have one thing in common: they are empty inside, with walls of equal thickness. That is exactly what „Wydrąż” does. Select the body and click „Wydrąż”, or right-click the body and pick it from the menu. Set the „Grubość ścianki”. Under „Otwarte strony”, switch on the sides that stay open: „Góra”, „Dół”, „Przód”, „Tył”, „Lewo” or „Prawo”, as many as you like - „Przód” alone makes a slot for a drawer, „Lewo” and „Prawo” a tunnel. With no side switched on the body stays closed all round, with a cavity in the middle. Decide whether the „Krawędzie wewnętrzne” should be „Zaokrąglone” or „Ostre”. Click „Wydrąż”. The hollowing panel with wall thickness, a switch for each side that stays open, and the inner edges. The walls grow inward. The outside stays as it is. The „Krawędzie wewnętrzne” only matter where the inner walls move apart - at a step in the body or around an opening. The corners of the cavity of a plain box are always sharp, with both settings. For a rounded inside, round the outside edges of the body first (see above), then hollow it: the inside follows with the radius minus the wall thickness. If the rounded inside cannot be built, which can happen with an outline made of very many short straight pieces such as a traced drawing, layerling builds the same hollow body with sharp inner corners instead. The result: a shell with a 3 mm wall, open at the top. The same box with only the front side open: a slot for a drawer. For every open side, the body needs a flat face at its very edge on that side. Spheres and free-form shapes therefore cannot be hollowed this way. If the wall is too thick for the body, layerling tells you and asks for a thinner one. A body with a pocket - a block with a hole that does not go all the way through, made by grouping a box with a raised hole - can be hollowed too, with the top open: the walls round the pocket are hollowed as well, so a ring of cavity stays between the outer wall and the pocket, open at the top, and a thin cavity lies under the pocket's floor. Bodies that end in a point, such as a cone or a revolved triangle, have no flat face on top that could stay open. A fully closed cavity does not work there either, because a point cannot be offset inwards: even with a 1 mm wall you get the message that the walls cannot be this thick. Draw the wall into the profile before revolving instead: duplicate the outline, scale the copy down evenly, put it in the middle of the large outline and cut the large one with it, then revolve the whole (chapter Sketches, section Revolve). The distance between the two outlines is the wall thickness. If you resize a hollowed body later, layerling hollows it again at the new size right away. The wall stays as thick as you chose, round bodies included. A cylinder you pull further one way than the other becomes an ellipse. Tip: With a 0.4 mm nozzle, 1.2 to 2 mm of wall is a good start: thin enough to save material, thick enough for a sturdy part.

Draw a flat outline, round or chamfer its corners and pull or spin it into a body. Not everything can be put together from basic shapes. For parts with a contour of their own, such as a bracket, a tooth profile or a vase, you first draw the outline and then make a body from it. That is what sketch mode is for.

At the top, switch from „Edytor 3D” to „Szkic”. Click „Szkic w 3D” in the ribbon and choose what the outline should become: „Wyciągnij szkic”: The outline is pulled upward, like a cookie cutter. „Obróć szkic”: The outline is spun about an axis, as on a lathe. That gives vases, cups, cones and everything round. The editor then shows a sheet with a grid. That is your drawing surface.

The ribbon in sketch mode is divided into areas: Draw: „Linia” makes straight sections: click points one after another; holding Shift snaps the new line in 15° steps, horizontal and vertical included. The length and angle of the new line show at the pointer. You can also type how long it should be, see Lines by numbers. The „Krzywa Béziera” is shaped with its handles: click a point and drag in the direction the line should carry on, as with the pen tool in Illustrator or Inkscape. The further you drag, the more it bends; the stretch to the new point bends along while you drag, so you see what you get. Dragging while you place a point bends the curve; if you come from Tinkercad and just want to click points, take the „Gładka krzywa”. The „Gładka krzywa” lays a flowing path through the points you click. To close the outline, click the first point again at the end. Shapes: „Dodaj kształt szkicu” offers ready-made outlines: „Prostokąt”, „Okrąg”, „Owal”, „Półokrąg”, „Wycinek koła”, „Okrąg otworów” (a disc with holes), „Trójkąt”, „Sześciokąt”, a „Wielokąt” and a „Gwiazda”. Click one to put it at the origin of the sketch, or drag it from the menu to where you want it. At the bottom of the menu, „Boki / ramiona” sets the number of sides of the polygon and of points of the star, and „Wymiar wewnętrzny gwiazdy” how deep the star's valleys reach in towards the middle (10 to 90 percent of the outer radius); both apply to the next shape you add. Like every sketch shape they are ordinary corner points afterwards, so you can move, round or chamfer them one by one. Overlapping: Push two closed outlines over each other and they stay two bodies, which merge in the 3D editor; the overlap is not a hole. A hole only comes from an outline lying wholly inside another. Moving does not join the lines where they cross, so you can pull the shapes apart again. If you draw a line across others, though, layerling puts a point at every crossing. Selection: „Zaznacz” moves points and lines. A click inside a closed outline selects the whole outline, so you can drag or resize it straight away; inside a hole it picks the hole. The frame around the selection has eight handles: the corners change width and height together, keeping the proportions while you hold Shift. The ones on the sides change one direction only. The round handle above the frame turns the whole selection about its middle: the figure over it shows the angle, and with Shift held it moves in steps of 15°. R turns a whole closed outline by 45° at each press. Click the width or height pill to type a new size, also as a sum ("60+12.5") or in percent ("150%"). With Shift held, a click on a point or line adds it to the selection or takes it away again, so you can pick several and move them together. Drag a box over empty space to select everything in it. A line can be dragged too (it moves by its two ends, or all of the selection if it is part of one). The arrow keys move the selection by one grid step, Shift with them by a larger one, and Shift held while you drag keeps the move on one axis. „Dodaj lub usuń punkty”: a click on a section adds a point, a click on a point removes it. Also there are „Wymaż” and inserting a template image („Dodaj obraz”). Clipboard: „Kopiuj”, „Wklej”, „Duplikuj” and „Usuń” work on the selected points, lines and images, as in the 3D editor; Ctrl+X cuts. Pasted and duplicated geometry lands next to the original with a 10 mm gap, on a free spot where it touches no existing line, so it never gets joined to what is already there. It stays selected, so you can drag it straight into place. History: „Cofnij w szkicu” and „Ponów w szkicu”. View: Pan it with the middle mouse button or with Shift or Ctrl plus the right mouse button, as in the 3D editor. F fits the whole sketch in the view, Shift+F zooms to the selection, and + and − zoom in and out, as in the 3D editor. The „Taśma miernicza” on the side bar measures the distance between two points. The sketch also shows dimensions as soon as you click something: the length of a line, or for a point the lengths of the lines that meet there. The „Pokaż wymiary” button on the side bar hides and shows these dimensions when they get in the way, for example while shaping curves; the tape measure keeps working. On a straight line you can click the dimension pill and type the length in millimetres; Enter applies it, Esc cancels. The line keeps its direction, its start point stays where it is, and the lines at the other end follow. With an end point selected, that one moves. Alt+Enter grows the line to both sides around its middle. On curves the pill only shows the length. A body comes only from a closed outline. An L-shaped outline. At the selected corner point, top left, the lengths of the two lines are shown in millimetres, and the angle between them in degrees.

Once you have set the first point with „Linia” or „Gładka krzywa”, just type a number: two fields open next to the line, „Długość” in millimetres and „Kąt” in degrees. < or Tab moves to the angle, so "50<30" gives a line 50 mm long at 30°, as in AutoCAD. Enter sets the point, and you can type the next line straight away; Esc closes the fields without ending the line chain. The angle counts counterclockwise from the right: 0° to the right, 90° up, 180° to the left, 270° down. Leave it empty and the line follows the pointer, so you give only the length and show the direction with the mouse. Sums like "40+12.5" work in both fields. If the point would land off the plate, the field says so and waits for another value.

Select a straight line and click „Wygnij linię” in the bar that appears: the side bows out into a curve, as in Tinkercad, and shows its two handles. Drag them to shape the curve; the further out a handle stands, the stronger the bend. „Linia prosta” makes the side straight again. A point you select can be made round with „Gładka krzywa”: it gets handles of its own and the lines next to it become curves. The bottom side of the L-shaped outline bent into a curve, with its two handles at the ends.

Click a corner point where two straight lines meet: next to the lengths, layerling shows the angle between them in degrees, with a small arc. On a closed outline it is the angle inside the shape, so a dent reads above 180°. Click the value and type a new angle. One of the two lines then turns about the corner and keeps its length, and the other stays where it is. The line that turns is drawn dashed; Tab switches to the other one, Enter applies and Esc cancels. What hangs at the far end of the turned line goes with it. Moving a point changes three angles: at the point itself and at the two neighbouring corners at the far ends of its lines. So layerling shows those two as well, and each can be clicked and typed. That way you set, say, the bottom left corner to 75.5° while the top left point, which moves for it, is selected. You can calculate here too, e.g. "90-14.5". A corner shows no angle where a curve meets it, or where more than two lines meet. The „Pokaż wymiary” button on the side bar hides the angle together with the lengths.

Click a corner point and choose „Zaokrąglij narożnik” or „Sfazuj narożnik”. A small field appears for the „Promień” or the „Odległość”. Enter the size and confirm with the check mark. This works for corners between two straight lines. Several corners at once work too: select them with Shift and a click each, or pull a frame round them, and choose „Zaokrąglij narożnik” or „Sfazuj narożnik” from the bar that appears. All of them get the same radius or distance. Where two selected corners share a side, each takes at most 45 % of it, so a rectangle rounded all round comes out alike at every corner. Points that are not a corner between two straight lines are left out, and the message says how many. A frame round a whole shape, or a click inside it, selects its corners and its lines together, and the bar then offers „Wygnij linię” and „Linia prosta” for all the selected lines next to the corner tools. The corner at the top left is rounded with a 12 mm radius.

A construction line helps you place points without becoming part of the body. It is drawn dashed and never counts as outline: you can pull it as far beyond the shape as you like and the body does not grow. Switch on „Linia konstrukcyjna” in the „Rysuj” group. New lines, those typed by measure too, are then construction lines. The button switches back to normal lines. A line you have drawn already becomes a construction line when you click it and choose „Konstrukcyjna”. „Zmień w linię” makes it a normal line again. New points snap to where a construction line crosses another line, a blue ring shows it, and to the ends of the construction line. That is how you put a corner on a middle, at a fixed distance from an edge or on a crossing, without calculating. A construction line does not cut the outline apart where it crosses it. When revolving it may lie to the right of the axis too.

Click „Zakończ szkic”. The outline stands as a body on the workplane. In its settings you change the height, the colour and everything else as with any other shape. When you resize it, layerling builds it again from the sketch a moment later, and the sketch grows with it. So it stays an exact body that takes chamfers and fillets, and the next time you edit it the sketch has the size the body has. If the workplane lies on the side of a body, you draw the way you look at that side: up in the sketch is up on the finished body too. The faint outline of the body in the sketch view shows where it stands. If the workplane cuts through a body, the sketch view shows the outline of that cut instead, so a hollow body appears as a ring and you can line the sketch up with its walls. A point you set or drag close to a corner of these outlines snaps exactly onto it; a small blue ring shows it. That way you take edges of other bodies into the sketch, even when the workplane does not lie exactly on them. The outline has become a body. The corner is rounded. With „Edytuj szkic” you can return to the sketch at any time to change it.
